newsitem.title: USA: Growing Miami deficit heightens rating concerns.
newsitem.headline: Growing Miami deficit heightens rating concerns.

text.p: Miami's increased estimate of its budget shortfall is cause for concern but probably will not result in immediate rating action, a municipal credit analyst said Wednesday.

Acting City Manager Merrett Stierheim said Tuesday the city has a $20 million shortfall in its capital budget in addition to the $40 million deficit previously announced in its operating budget, putting the total shortfall for fiscal 1997 at about $60 million.
"Obviously this heightens our concerns," said John Incorvaia, a vice president at Moody's Investors Service.
Moody's put its single-A rating for Miami's general obligation bonds under review with negative implications last week, citing the budget mess.
Incorvaia said Moody's still had numerous questions, such as whether any of the capital obligations were to be funded with general fund revenues and whether any capital expenditures could be delayed.
He said no further rating action was imminent, "as long as we're still comfortable" that the city has set aside adequate revenues to make debt service payments.
"We want to give them time to come up with a plan," he said.

An analyst at Standard & Poor's said its single-A rating of Miami GO debt was under review in connection with the city's upcoming issue of tax anticipation notes. She said she could not comment further on Miami's credit rating until after the issue goes before S&P's rating committee.
Fitch Investors Service does not rate any Miami debt.
